title: Multi-agent tasks: which coding agent
how_to_use: For task class X use classes.X.first_choice; if it cannot run right now, take the next entry in fallbacks. For coding and agentic work, use classes.X.subclasses.Y instead when the task is clearly kind Y. Take entries in the order listed: the order is the ranking. With few own jobs, the evidence and tie rules can put a lower score first. Field definitions: method.fields. The short form of this file is /bench.md.

method.own_success: own_success: a weekly random sample of jobs graded against their own instructions (pass 1, partial 0.5, fail 0) once a pair has enough graded jobs, else the share of jobs that finished cleanly.
method.cost: cost_rank: estimated list-price cost per successful job, cheapest 1, dearest 0 (inverted min-max over log cost across the class's candidates); cheaper wins when quality is close. Estimate from own jobs when a pair has 3 or more successful ones in the class (cost_source 'own jobs'), else the model's blended list price times the engine's typical job size ('list price'), else 0.5 ('default').
method.cost_tier: cost_tier: $ to $$$$, the model's blended list price (3 input : 1 output tokens) in four log-spaced bins from the cheapest to the dearest ranked model. Prices: OpenRouter model list.
method.effort: effort: the reasoning effort to run the entry at. Default: Claude Code Fable medium, Opus medium, Sonnet medium, Haiku high; Codex and Grok their CLI config (marked config); Antigravity the -high model id. A public leaderboard that scores the same model at several effort levels moves it only when another level beats the default by at least 0.03 on the class's normalized public score (marked with the source).
method.evidence_rule: Proven means at least 5 own jobs in the window. An unproven entry ranks above a proven one only if its priority is more than 0.03 higher and its public_norm is higher; never on cost or speed alone. Quality before cost: an unproven entry leads only if its public_norm is within 0.05 of the best in the pool.
method.harness_rule: A public metric measured in another agent's harness counts at 0.8x (norm multiplied). The engine's own harness, or a model-only benchmark (no harness or a neutral one), counts in full.
method.subclasses: Coding and agentic subclasses are ranked the same way, on the public metrics that measure that kind of work and own jobs of that kind; a subclass with neither is not listed.
method.effort_evidence: classes.X.effort_evidence: benchmark_steps = the score gained between two effort levels a board publishes for one model (from effort_charts; gain in the board's own unit); own_jobs = own jobs of one model that ran at two or more effort levels with at least 5 jobs each (jobs, finished cleanly, median turns and median output tokens of the finished ones). Own jobs are not a controlled test: the effort was chosen per job. own_levels = every engine, model and effort level with at least that many own jobs in the class (the same four figures), shown beside the model's Artificial Analysis points. cost_step = for the highest-ranked model in the class that Artificial Analysis scores at the next effort level up from the one it runs at here: the index gained and the list-price cost per task at both levels. Cost per effort level comes from one source, Artificial Analysis (cost_curve: USD per task of its Intelligence Index at API list price, not the cost of our jobs); no source gives tokens per effort level.
method.cost_curve: cost_curve: per model and reasoning effort level, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (index) and what running that index cost per task in USD at API list price (cost_per_task), with the median end-to-end response time in seconds where the API has it. One point per record of Artificial Analysis's free API; ranked models, plus up to three unranked models with two or more levels (ranked false). It feeds no score.

status_meanings.proven: at least 5 own jobs of this kind in the last 28 days
status_meanings.unproven: fewer than 5 own jobs: ranked on public scores
status_meanings.probation: a new version of a model: for its first 28 days it counts its predecessor's own jobs with its own (at least 5 together), and the predecessor's public scores until the leaderboards list it

fields.priority: 0-1, higher is better: the entry's score (method.formula). It does not alone set the order; see rank_rule.
fields.rank_rule: null = placed by priority; 'tie' = within method.tie_band of a neighbour and ordered by method.tie_order; 'evidence' = placed by method.evidence_rule (proven before unproven). tie_broken is true when rank_rule is 'tie'.
fields.status: a list holding one of proven, unproven, probation (method.status_meanings).
fields.successor_of: only on probation entries: the model whose own jobs and public scores this one inherits.
fields.public_norm: 0-1, higher is better: the mean of the entry's public_metrics norm values, each scaled across the class's candidates and multiplied by harness_factor. 0.5 when public_default is true.
fields.public_default: true = the model has no public metric for this class, so public_norm is the placeholder 0.5.
fields.public_metrics: keyed by feed metric id (sources[].metric). source = the sources[].slug it comes from, where its unit and snapshot date (as_of) are; score = the published value; level = the reasoning effort the leaderboard entry names (null = none named), which can differ from the effort the entry is run at here; leaderboard_name = the entry's name on the leaderboard; norm = 0-1 after the harness factor, norm_before_discount before it; harness_relation = own, other or model-only; harness = the agent harness the score was measured in ('' = none); source_url = the leaderboard entry or page; inherited_from = the predecessor whose score this is.
fields.metrics_used: the metrics the class or kind reads; a model may have a value for none of them.
fields.own_success: 0-1, higher is better: the score input (method.own_success). 0.5 when own_success_default is true (fewer than method.min_jobs_for_own_success own jobs).
fields.own_success_rate: 0-1: the share of own jobs that finished cleanly; null with no own jobs. Completion, not quality.
fields.own_jobs: own jobs of this engine, model and class (or kind) in the last method.own_outcomes_window_days days.
fields.own_median_minutes: median wall-clock minutes of those jobs; null with no own jobs.
fields.speed_rank: 0-1, higher is faster: rank by own_median_minutes across the class's candidates; 0.5 when speed_source is 'default'.
fields.cost_rank: 0-1, higher is cheaper (method.cost). 0.5 when cost_default is true.
fields.cost_tier: $ to $$$$ (method.cost_tier); null when no price is known.
fields.price_blended_per_mtok: US dollars per million tokens at list price, 3 input : 1 output.
fields.effort: the reasoning effort to run the entry at; effort_source = 'default' (the standing default), 'config' (the CLI's own config) or the name of the leaderboard whose scores moved it (method.effort).
fields.model: this site's key for the model; engines.X.models lists the keys each CLI runs. The CLI's own model id can be spelled differently.
fields.cost_curve: series[].points[]: level = reasoning effort; index = Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (higher is better); cost_per_task = US dollars per task of that index at API list price (lower is cheaper; not the cost of a coding job or of our jobs); seconds = median end-to-end response time per response. source = a sources[].slug. ranked false = a comparison model not ranked here. inherited_from = the predecessor whose points these are.
fields.cost_chart: what the chart at the top of the page plots, kept in every build so an earlier week can be redrawn: as_of = the source snapshot date; points = every plotted point (model, level, index, cost_per_task as in cost_curve), for the models the routing table names; frontier = the points no other point beats on both index and cost, cheapest first; previous = the frontier of the build named in previous.build (the one `changes` compares with), absent when that build kept no points.
fields.cost_steps: from cost_curve, for every ranked model: each step between two neighbouring published effort levels. gain = to_index - from_index; cost_ratio = to_cost / from_cost, rounded to one decimal.
fields.effort_evidence: per class (method.effort_evidence). benchmark_steps[].model is a display name. own_jobs is a regrouping of own_levels. finished = jobs that ended cleanly (completion, not quality). median_turns is not comparable across engines. summary and summary_lead are display text.
fields.sources: metric = the feed metric id that keys public_metrics (a trailing * is a prefix; null for own jobs). in_score = whether the source counts in priority today. weight is display text. as_of = the snapshot date (the text 'rolling 28 days' for own jobs; the window ends at data_dates.generated_at). harness_factor applies only to a score measured in another agent's harness. models_covered = ranked models with a value (0 = it changes nothing today; null for own jobs). kinds are 'class / kind'.
fields.base_data: keyed by model key, then by source name (sources[].name): raw = the highest published value in `unit`, rounded for display; level = the effort level of that value; variants = every level published. effort_charts is keyed by sources[].slug. A level of null means the source names no effort level; the level 'none' means reasoning switched off.
fields.engines: models = the model keys the CLI runs; models_verified false = the list was not checked against the CLI; not_listed = models the CLI no longer offers.
fields.data_dates: generated_at = when this file was built (UTC); sources_oldest and sources_newest = the range of source snapshot dates (sources[].as_of); own_jobs_window_days and own_jobs_window_end = the own-job window; rebuilt = how often the file is rebuilt; history = the dated list of earlier builds.
fields.changes: first choices that differ from the build named in compared_to (the newest build at least 6 days older; null = none to compare with). kind null = the class row. Engine and model only.

sources.name: Terminal-Bench 4.0
description: Each task gives an agent an instruction and its own environment; the agent works in the terminal, and a verifier's tests decide whether the task was done.
Scored as accuracy over trials, with at least 5 trials per task; errored trials count as failures, and an LLM judge reviews successful trials for reward hacking.
A submission is one agent harness, model and reasoning effort together, so a score says as much about the harness as the model; we count a score from another agent's harness at 0.8x.

sources.name: SWE-bench Verified
description: A model, inside an agent scaffold, gets a GitHub issue and its repository and has to produce a patch that fixes it.
Scored as the percentage of tasks resolved, out of 500 SWE-bench tasks that human annotators checked for clear problem statements and correct tests.
The standard test for fixing bugs in existing code. Caveat: entries are a model plus a scaffold, and the board had no recent entries for most models we rank.

sources.name: SWE-bench Multilingual
sources.measures: repo issues resolved in nine languages
description: SWE-bench-style tasks in other languages: 300 tasks from 42 repositories in C, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Ruby and Rust.
A task counts as resolved when the patch passes two sets of unit tests taken from the original pull request.
Would tell us about repo work outside Python. Caveat: none of the models we rank has an entry yet, so it affects no ranking today.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis coding index
description: A single coding score per model that Artificial Analysis publishes in its API, from its own runs of coding evaluations.
Its methodology page does not list which evaluations make up this index, so we do not describe its parts.
Not in use: Artificial Analysis's free API returns no value for this index (checked 12 Nov 2026), so no model has one here.
sources.note: not in Artificial Analysis's free API

sources.name: Arena Text: coding
description: People ask a question in Arena's battle mode, see answers from two anonymous models side by side and vote for the better one; this board keeps only prompts Arena classifies as coding.
Ratings come from a Bradley-Terry fit to those votes, published as the Arena score.
Shows whose coding answers people prefer in chat. Caveat: preference in a chat answer, not whether the code runs in a repository.

sources.name: Arena WebDev
sources.measures: people's votes on built web apps
description: Code Arena: two anonymous models build a web app or page from the same request and people vote on the result; Arena describes it as full-stack web development with multi-step reasoning, tool use and end-to-end app generation.
Rated from the votes and published as the Arena score; one model can appear at two reasoning efforts.
Our best signal for frontend and UI work. Caveat: it judges the finished app as people see it, not the code behind it.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis agentic index
description: A single agentic score per model that Artificial Analysis publishes in its API.
Its methodology page does not list which evaluations make up this index, so we do not describe its parts.
Not in use: Artificial Analysis's free API returns no value for this index (checked 12 Nov 2026), so no model has one here.
sources.note: not in Artificial Analysis's free API

sources.name: Arena Agent: bash reliability
sources.measures: shell work in real agent sessions
description: A shell-command signal from Agent Arena, which analyses real sessions of people using Agent Mode on arena.ai for their own work.
Published as an IPS score with a 95% confidence interval; Arena's methodology post does not define this particular signal, so we do not describe how it is counted.
Feeds terminal and sysadmin work. Caveat: the sessions run in Arena's own agent, on whatever tasks its users bring.

sources.name: Arena Agent: bash recovery
sources.measures: recovering from a failed shell command
description: After a shell command errors in a real Agent Mode session, how many more turns the agent takes to reach a command that runs; giving up is penalised.
Published as an IPS score with a 95% confidence interval.
Feeds terminal and sysadmin work. Caveat: measured in Arena's own agent, on its users' tasks.

sources.name: Arena Agent: tool calls
sources.measures: not calling tools that do not exist
description: In real Agent Mode sessions, a task is marked a failure when the agent calls a tool that does not exist.
Published as an IPS score with a 95% confidence interval; the spread between models is small.
Feeds tool and connector workflows. Caveat: it catches invented tools, not wrong arguments to real ones.

sources.name: Arena Agent: task outcome
description: At the end of a real Agent Mode session the user marks the task a success or a failure in Arena's interface.
Published as an IPS score with a 95% confidence interval.
Feeds tool and connector workflows. Caveat: each user judges their own task, in Arena's agent.

sources.name: DeepResearch Bench
description: 100 PhD-level research tasks (50 in Chinese, 50 in English) across 22 fields, written by domain experts; a system writes a full research report for each.
Reports are judged by RACE, which compares them with reference reports using an LLM judge, and FACT, which checks how many citations are effective and accurate; we read the leaderboard's total score.
Would tell us about deep research. Caveat: most entries are research products, not the models we rank, and none of ours has an entry.

sources.name: Arena Search
description: Arena's leaderboard for searching the web: people compare two anonymous models' answers side by side and vote.
Rated with a Bradley-Terry fit to the votes, published as the Arena score.
Feeds research. Caveat: few of the models we rank have an entry.

sources.name: Arena Document
sources.measures: people's votes on answers about PDFs
description: People upload a PDF, ask about it, and compare two anonymous models' answers side by side.
Rated with a Bradley-Terry fit to the votes, published as the Arena score.
Feeds reading. Caveat: questions about one uploaded document, not reading across many files.

sources.name: Arena Text: creative writing
description: Arena Text battles in the creative writing category: two anonymous answers, and people vote for the one they prefer.
Rated with a Bradley-Terry fit to the votes, published as the Arena score.
Feeds writing. Caveat: taste in short chat answers; it says nothing about long documents or a house style.

sources.name: Arena Text
sources.measures: people's votes on all text prompts
description: All Arena Text battles: people see answers from two anonymous models side by side and vote for the better one.
Rated with a Bradley-Terry fit to the votes, published as the Arena score; we use the raw ratings, not the style-controlled ones.
Feeds writing as a general quality signal. Caveat: a broad mix of everyday prompts, specific to no one task.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5
sources.measures: overall index, per effort level, with cost per task
description: One overall score per model that Artificial Analysis publishes from its own runs of a set of evaluations.
Its free API lists a model once per reasoning effort level, each with the index and what running the index cost at API list price, in total and per task; it gives no token counts.
Not part of any score here: shown for its effort and cost curves. Caveat: one general index, specific to no kind of task, and its cost is list price for the index's own tasks.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis output speed
description: How fast a model streams its answer: tokens received per second after the first token, measured on the same endpoint Artificial Analysis uses for price.
Higher is faster; we would scale it across the models we rank.

Meant as a fallback when we have no timings of our own. Fetched and shown since 12 Nov 2026 but not counted yet: the free API reports one speed per reasoning effort level, and the score does not yet choose a level.

sources.name: OpenRouter prices
description: The per-token prices OpenRouter lists for each model, taken from the top provider for that model, in US dollars.
We blend 3 input tokens to 1 output token and show dollars per million tokens; lower is cheaper.
Sets the $ to $$$$ tier, and the cost estimate when we have fewer than 3 priced jobs of our own. Caveat: one provider's list price, which can differ from the model maker's own price.

sources.name: Own jobs
sources.measures: our own dispatched jobs over 28 days
description: The jobs we hand to these agents in our own work, counted per engine and model for each task class and kind.

Own success is the share that finished cleanly or, once a pair has enough graded jobs, the mean grade from a weekly random sample graded against each job's own instructions; median minutes and list-price cost also count.
Only aggregate counts and rates are published, never the jobs themselves. Caveat: our own task mix, not a general benchmark.

bugfix.description: finding and fixing defects in existing code

frontend.description: web pages, UI components and styling

multilang.description: repo work outside Python: JS/TS, Go, Rust, Java, PHP

effort_evidence.summary: Claude Sonnet 5.5, medium to high: +10.7 on the Artificial Analysis index (30.8 to 41.5) for 2.1 times the list-price cost per task ($0.78 to $1.64); it is the first choice here, and the index is general, not this kind of task. Boards: medium to high gives +6 Arena score on Arena Text: coding (Gemini 3.5 Flash, not ranked here); above high, +58 Arena score on Arena WebDev (Claude Sonnet 5.5, high to xhigh); +1 Arena score on Arena Text: coding (Claude Opus 5, not ranked here, high to max); and 3 more; cost per level comes only from Artificial Analysis (list price per task), and no source gives tokens. Our jobs (Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code): 71 of 74 finished cleanly at medium, 51 of 51 at high; on the jobs each level was given (not the same jobs), median output tokens were 59,416 at medium and 59,958 at high.
